title: Trace the stack
prompt: `push(1); push(2); pop(); push(3);` — what does `peek()` return, and what's still inside?
options: peek is 3; the stack holds [1, 3] (bottom to top)
explanation: pop removed the 2. LIFO: the most recent push is always what peek/pop see.

title: Stack and queue vocabulary
explanation: push/pop for stacks, offer/poll for queues. Same ArrayDeque class, different ends.

title: Recall: both ends of a Deque
prompt: Fill in the double-ended operations. Use the explicit `First`/`Last` names.
code:
Deque<Integer> dq = new ArrayDeque<>();
dq.{{1}}(1);              // add to the FRONT
dq.{{2}}(2);              // add to the BACK
int front = dq.{{3}}();   // remove + return the front
int back = dq.{{4}}();    // look at the back (don't remove)
explanation: Front: `offerFirst` / `pollFirst` / `peekFirst`. Back: `offerLast` / `pollLast` / `peekLast`. The shorthands map onto these: `push` = add to front, `pop` and `poll` = remove from front, `offer` = add to back. Only the back has no shorthand for peeking, so `peekLast` it is.

title: Reverse via stack
prompt: Return a new array with the elements of `nums` reversed — by pushing everything onto a stack, then popping into the result. (Deliberately not the two-pointer way: the point is feeling LIFO reverse order.)

solution.explanation: Everything that goes through a stack comes out reversed — the property monotonic-stack problems exploit.

hints: Whatever goes into a stack comes out in reverse order.
Push all, then pop into `res[0], res[1], ...`

title: Drill: matching pairs
prompt: From memory — a mini Valid Parentheses: given a string of only `(` and `)`, return whether it's balanced. Push `(`; on `)`, if the stack is empty return false, else pop. Balanced = stack empty at the end. (A counter works too, but drill the stack shape — you'll need it for the 3-bracket version.)

solution.explanation: Two failure modes: closing with nothing open (mid-loop check) and opening without closing (final isEmpty check).

hints: Every `)` must match the most recent unmatched `(`.
Return false immediately if you see `)` with an empty stack.

title: Recall: stack (Deque)
prompt: Fill in the stack operations on an ArrayDeque.
code:
Deque<Integer> stack = new ArrayDeque<>();
stack.{{1}}(5);              // add to top
int top = stack.{{2}}();     // look at top (don't remove)
stack.{{3}}();               // remove the top
boolean e = stack.{{4}}();   // empty?
explanation: For a stack, use `push`/`pop`/`peek` on an `ArrayDeque` (not the legacy `Stack` class).

title: Drill: top after pushing all
prompt: From memory: push every element of `nums` (non-empty) onto a stack, then return the top with `peek`.

solution.explanation: A stack is LIFO, so after pushing all values the top is the last one pushed. `peek` reads it without removing it. O(n).

hints: Which element does a stack expose: the first pushed, or the last?

title: Recall: queue
code:
Queue<Integer> q = new ArrayDeque<>();
q.{{1}}(5);              // add to back
int front = q.{{2}}();   // look at front
q.{{3}}();               // remove the front
explanation: For a queue, `offer` adds to the back and `poll` removes from the front (FIFO); `peek` looks at the front.

title: Drill: through the queue
prompt: From memory: offer every element of `nums` into a queue, then poll them all into a result array. FIFO means the order is unchanged.

solution.explanation: FIFO preserves order: values leave in the same order they entered. `ArrayDeque` gives O(1) `offer` and `poll`, so the whole thing is O(n).

hints: A queue is FIFO: the first value in is the first out.
`offer` all, then `poll` in a loop into `res`.
